messages:
incidents-bot: PAGER -> prod: high GPU queue growth detected in us-west-2, autoscale hit max (max_replicas=120). Throttling observed. Paging oncall.
Jane (oncall SRE): I'm on it. first glance: scheduler logs show a lot of Pending pods waiting for 16Gi MIG slices.
Mike (runtime): confirming - serving runtime telemetry shows token queue up ~18k requests, tail latency spiking >12s. Some backpressure from prefix cache misses.
Luis (allocation): autoscaler metric shows scaling attempts failed due to capacity fragmentation: many nodes have leftover GPU memory slices < slice size. MIG-size mismatch across pools.
Hana (prod-support): Any customer visible errors? Support ticket #33214 reports timeouts for two high-throughput customers.
Carla (ops): I can run a manual reprioritize to evict batch jobs. Do we want emergency reclaim of low-priority pools? :warning:
Jane (oncall SRE): yes, please start evicting low-priority/spot jobs now. Luis, can you try a manual scale-up beyond max as emergency? We can roll back after.
Luis (allocation): Trying override via allocator API: `POST /allocator/v1/scale?force=true&target=150` — request queued.
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline note: ramping extra instances may interact with packing controller. Keep an eye.
Mike (runtime): While scale-up kicks, we should throttle non-critical customers at edge. Applying temporary rate-limit policy for groups tag=nonpaying.
Hana (prod-support): Notifying affected customers now: "We are experiencing degraded response times in US-WEST; mitigation in progress." Will post timeline update after 30min.
Jane (oncall SRE): Getting k8s describe for one Pending pod:
```
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m (x12 over 18m)  default-scheduler  0/120 nodes are available: 70 Insufficient gpu, 50 Insufficient mig.iso-size.
```
Mike (runtime): That matches: binpack prefers uniform MIG slices; fragments across nodes cause inability to place new pods even if aggregate GPUs available.
Carla (ops): Started eviction: `kubectl cordon node-spot-42 && kubectl drain node-spot-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` for three nodes, pushing batch off.
Frank (incident commander): Setting Sev=2. Need ETA for customer recovery and RCA tasks. Also please track which customers impacted and whether any SLAs breached.
Luis (allocation): Scale override succeeded: allocator accepted request, starting provisioning of +30 slices (target 150). Provisioning ETA ~7m.
Mike (runtime): Runtime reports new workers registering. Queue dropping slowly. Tail latency tracing shows a hot path on KV cache misses; we'll keep tracing.
Jane (oncall SRE): Manual repack attempt: triggering force-repack job to consolidate fragments.
```
curl -XPOST https://internal-api/repack -d '{"force":true, "binpack":"aggressive"}'
```
Carla (ops): Force-repack started; may cause short-term pod churn as we move shards. Expected churn window 2-3m.
Hana (prod-support): Update to customers: "We expect restoration to normal in ~10-15 minutes; partial workarounds applied." :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Mike (runtime): Noting a recurring pattern: older clusters have mixed MIG sizes (1g,2g,4g) due to historical onboarding. Model footprints now prefer 4g slices leading to stranded 1g/2g fragments.
Luis (allocation): After repack + new capacity, placement success rate increased from 28% -> 82% for Pending pod class.
Jane (oncall SRE): Still seeing ~2k queue, but steady decline. Monitoring for regressions for next 30m.
Frank (incident commander): Good. Produce an incident channel summary for customers + postmortem. Assign owners: Luis=allocation RCA, Mike=runtime perf trace, Carla=ops repack playbook update, Jane=mitigation timeline and runbook update.
Hana (prod-support): Logged impacted customers: Acme AI (timeouts), Streamlytics (elevated latency). CS notified and offered credits if SLA breaches confirmed.
Mike (runtime): Short-term follow-ups: implement binpack affinity hints for model-serving pods, and add a preflight check that refuses placement if fragmentation > 60%.
Luis (allocation): Long-term: propose homogenizing MIG sizes for new pools and an auto-resize routine to convert stranded 1g/2g to 4g where node hardware allows.
Carla (ops): Will add forced repack as a rescue action to ops runbook and include safe drain steps.
Jane (oncall SRE): Last action: remove emergency override once queue < 500 and tail latency < 2s sustained for 10m.
deploy-bot: action log: allocator.scale override remained active; manual revoke scheduled at 5299994020 unless canceled.
Frank (incident commander): Handing off to morning oncall. Severity will remain open until RCA posted. Thanks all for rapid response. :tada:
Hana (prod-support): Leaving final customer note in 15m after verification.
Jane (oncall SRE): Handoff note: I've created follow-ups in Jira (INC-4678) and booked a postmortem doc. Oncall next: @next-oncall. Signed off, handing to day team.
Carla (ops): Dropping a quick checklist in #runbooks: "Emergency repack and temporary scale override".
Mike (runtime): We'll add a sampling eval to detect models that cause fragmentation due to unexpected memory growth.
Frank (incident commander): Incident channel will remain archived after postmortem. Closing this thread once RCA and runbook changes done.
